verdict.rationale: Community users report that GitLab is open source at its core, so anyone can run or fork their own instance. First-party docs indirectly confirm the source is available: GitLab can be self-compiled, and the raw OpenAPI spec lives in the GitLab monorepo. No first-party evidence names the license or says which parts are open, and 'at its core' suggests not all of it is. Missing for 10: first-party statement of the open-source license, public source repository link, clarity on which editions/features are openly licensed.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: One user values that GitLab is open source at its core: anybody can run their own instance, and if the company moves in a direction the community dislikes, it can be forked.
Advocates say GitLab's open-source core is the key difference from GitHub: anyone can run their own instance or fork it
If the Linux package isn't available for your distribution, you can self-compile GitLab.
The raw OpenAPI 3.0 specification is available in the GitLab monorepo
